meta.name: Problem #3 canary set: The Model Changed Without Changing Its Name
meta.design: 81 synthetic canaries: 9 divisions x 3 cost tiers x 3 tasks. No production/user prompts are accepted or stored.
meta.token_estimates: est_in_tokens is a heuristic planning estimate over system + prompt + expanded filler. est_out_tokens is a design estimate. est_total_tokens is their sum. These are not billing values; replace with provider-reported usage after baseline runs.
meta.refusal_detection: Refusal classifier = regex on refusal phrases (I can't / I cannot / I'm unable / I won't / can't help with) in the first 200 characters, plus finish_reason == content_filter if the provider reports it.
meta.implementation: Go-first. Canary definitions and checks are JSON data; execution, checks, statistics, attribution and reporting are implemented in Go.
meta.task_identity: Each task id is stable. The runner generates a unique run_id and probe_execution_id for every execution; never reuse these identifiers.
meta.privacy: Only this synthetic canary set may be sent to providers. Never route production/user prompts through the canary runner. Persist synthetic prompt/response text only; production content is out of scope.
meta.style_analysis: No embedding model is required in v1. Use a normalized lexical/structural feature vector and compare it with the per-task baseline distribution. Embedding analysis is an optional later extension.

pricing_per_million_tokens.note: Configure current provider pricing per exact model outside the canary definitions. If unset, report token usage but do not estimate monetary cost.

easy.role: Cheap, high-frequency tripwires; repeated samples support proportion-rate monitoring.

general.role: Mid-cost probes with richer structural, capability and style signals.

expensive.schedule: every 4th cycle; also run as targeted follow-up probes after lower tiers flag a change
expensive.role: Long-input/output probes for truncation, throughput, extended style and token-count diagnostics.

divisions.name: 1. Refusal behaviour
divisions.why: All prompts are borderline-but-safe, so the baseline answer rate is high. A rise in refusals with flat accuracy and flat latency points to safety settings.

divisions.name: 2. Format compliance
divisions.why: Strict JSON, bullets, tables, CSV and outlines. A response_format change moves all of these together; a model change moves them unevenly.

divisions.name: 3. Determinism
divisions.why: Same prompt at temperature 0, repeated. Prompts have many valid answers, so a temperature change or numeric drift in serving shows up as divergence.

divisions.name: 4. Capability (known answers)
divisions.why: Math, extraction and sorting with exact answer keys. Accuracy moving while refusals and latency stay flat is a model signal.

divisions.name: 5. Style and voice
divisions.why: Open-ended writing. Embedding distance to the baseline centroid and length statistics catch silent model swaps that still pass accuracy checks.

divisions.name: 6. Latency and throughput
divisions.why: Fixed-length outputs make latency and output-token count comparable run to run. Latency shifting with unchanged content points to serving.

divisions.name: 7. Truncation and stop behaviour
divisions.why: Each task ends with a <<END>> sentinel and has about 1.5x token headroom. A lowered max_tokens produces finish_reason=length and a missing sentinel.

divisions.name: 8. Instruction and system-prompt adherence
divisions.why: Each task has a system prompt with checkable rules. A changed or dropped system prompt breaks the rules while capability stays flat.

divisions.name: 9. Token-count fingerprint
divisions.why: Fixed inputs with a trivial output ('OK'). Reported input_tokens is deterministic. A constant offset across all tasks suggests a hidden prompt or wrapper; a content-dependent shift suggests a tokenizer or serving change.

check_types.not_refused: Pass only when refusal classifier returns not_refusal; ambiguous is not a pass.
check_types.contains_all: Case-insensitive: every string in values[] must occur in the normalized response.
check_types.contains_any: Case-insensitive: at least one string in values[] must occur.
check_types.contains_none: Case-insensitive: none of the strings in values[] may occur.
check_types.regex_full: Regular expression must match the entire trimmed response.
check_types.output_equals: Trimmed response equals value; case-sensitive unless the checker explicitly defines otherwise.
check_types.number_equals: Extract the first number, or the number after ANSWER: when specified by checker implementation; compare numerically.
check_types.number_in_set: Extract the first number and check membership in values[].
check_types.final_field: Find a line beginning with label and compare its trimmed value to equals.
check_types.final_field_json: Parse JSON after label; compare expected fields (or expected_unordered arrays) and enforce must_exclude.
check_types.json_valid: The entire trimmed response parses as one JSON value; no surrounding prose or markdown fences.
check_types.json_fields: Parse JSON object and compare only the expected key/value pairs; other keys are allowed unless strict=true.
check_types.json_array: Parse JSON array; enforce length and optional id_sequence.
check_types.json_types: Validate JSON types, array lengths, allowed values and word constraints specified in the check.
check_types.no_code_fence: Response contains no Markdown code-fence markers.
check_types.bullet_count: Count top-level Markdown bullet lines and compare to value.
check_types.line_count: Count non-empty output lines and compare to value.
check_types.paragraph_count: Count non-empty paragraphs separated by one or more blank lines.
check_types.paragraph_count_max: Enforce maximum paragraph count; optional after field identifies a prefix/summary to exclude.
check_types.sentence_count: Count sentences using documented deterministic punctuation rules; abbreviations are a known limitation.
check_types.sentences_per_paragraph: Enforce the specified sentence count in every non-empty paragraph.
check_types.word_count_between: Word count is inclusive between min and max.
check_types.bullet_words_max: Every bullet must contain <= value words.
check_types.summary_words_max: Word count of the summary section must be <= value.
check_types.markdown_table: Validate Markdown table column count, data row count and optional no_text_outside_table.
check_types.table_cells: Validate specified row labels and expected cell values in a parsed Markdown table.
check_types.csv_shape: Parse CSV; validate column count, data row count, date bounds and allowed cell values.
check_types.outline_shape: Validate numbered sections, lettered sub-points and specified word-count range.
check_types.day_list_shape: Validate day count, required labels, bullet word limits and no-introduction rule.
check_types.all_lowercase: All alphabetic characters in the trimmed response must be lowercase.
check_types.language_is: Detect response language and compare to value; implementation must document detector and confidence threshold.
check_types.identical_across_runs: Aggregate checker: exact normalized responses are identical across repeated executions of the same task/config.
check_types.mean_edit_distance: Aggregate checker: calculate mean normalized pairwise edit distance across repeated responses for the same task/config.
check_types.style_feature_distance: Aggregate/baseline checker: compare pure-Go lexical/structural feature vector to the same task baseline; no embedding service required.
check_types.output_length_stats: Aggregate/baseline checker: compare word and provider-token count distributions with the same task baseline.
check_types.finish_reason: Compare normalized provider finish_reason to value; unknown/missing is recorded as unavailable, not silently treated as failure.
check_types.latency: Aggregate/baseline checker: compare client-observed latency distribution to same task baseline.
check_types.output_tokens_stable: Aggregate/baseline checker: compare provider-reported output token distribution to same task baseline.
check_types.input_tokens_stable: Aggregate/baseline checker: compare provider-reported input token counts for identical serialized requests; do not infer tokenizer identity from this alone.

development.description: Fast local iteration; not suitable for statistical conclusions.

deep_analysis.description: Investigation profile after a suspected change. Run all tiers immediately.

refusal_detection.primary_method: Go lexical rules over the full normalized response, not only the first 200 characters.

strong_refusal_patterns: I am unable to help with

rules: Strong refusal pattern plus no substantive answer => refusal.
Contextual phrase alone is insufficient; inspect whether a substantive answer follows.
A refusal phrase quoted or discussed as an example is not automatically a refusal.
Provider content-filter finish reason is a separate signal and must be retained even if lexical classification differs.
Ambiguous cases are excluded from binary refusal-rate numerator/denominator and reported separately until reviewed.
refusal_detection.note: A deterministic lexical classifier is a practical v1 approximation, not semantic ground truth. Validate against a manually labelled synthetic test set.

style_feature_spec.name: style_feature_vector_v1
style_feature_spec.normalization: Normalize each feature using the baseline mean and standard deviation for the same task; cap extreme z-scores to avoid one feature dominating.
style_feature_spec.distance: Euclidean distance over normalized features (or weighted Euclidean distance with documented fixed weights).
style_feature_spec.caution: Compare the same canary task against its own baseline; do not compare unrelated prompts as if their style distributions were interchangeable.

measurement_rules.unit_of_comparison: Same task_id + same requested model + same serialized request configuration + same provider route where possible.
measurement_rules.baseline: Maintain per-task baseline distributions. Baseline collection must include repeated observations over multiple independent cycles.
measurement_rules.request_identity: Hash canonicalized system prompt, user prompt, model, temperature, max_tokens, response_format and other generation parameters. Exclude secrets/API keys.
measurement_rules.latency: Use client-observed wall-clock latency; record retries separately. Compare like-for-like concurrency and route conditions.
measurement_rules.tokens: Use provider-reported usage when available. Missing usage is null/unavailable, not zero.
measurement_rules.multiple_testing: Apply Benjamini-Hochberg correction across metrics within a monitoring cycle; retain raw p-values and adjusted q-values.
measurement_rules.alerts: Require both statistical evidence and a minimum practical effect size. Tune thresholds using baseline-vs-baseline runs.
measurement_rules.attribution: Treat signature scores as ranked evidence, not calibrated probabilities. Return inconclusive when evidence is weak, conflicting or multiple layers are plausible.
measurement_rules.combined_changes: Support multi-label or inconclusive attribution; do not force exactly one layer when injected changes are combined.

provider_adapter_contract.request: Send only the synthetic system/prompt/filler content plus declared generation parameters.
provider_adapter_contract.normalization: Normalize provider-specific finish reasons and usage fields into a common internal result while retaining the raw provider values.
provider_adapter_contract.missing_fields: Represent unavailable metadata as null with an availability flag; never fabricate values.
provider_adapter_contract.retries: Record every retry and distinguish the final response from failed attempts; retry policy must be identical between baseline and monitoring.

validation.note: Tier mismatch is a planning warning. Review after first provider-reported token-usage run; do not automatically move tasks without considering intended diagnostic cost.

schema_contract.unknown_check_type: Reject canary file during validation; do not silently skip unknown checks.
schema_contract.invalid_task: Reject invalid task before any provider request is sent.
